author: Racheal Clark
title: Groesbeck Girls Softball Teams Chase State Titles - NewsBreak
text: The 15U Groesbeck Girls Softball team, Groesbeck Magic, will battle for a state title next week in a tournament taking place on their home turf. A victory would mark the first state championship in softball for Groesbeck since 2015. The 16-team tournament kicks off on Monday, June 30, and runs through the week, culminating in the final game at noon on July 4. Head Coach Sebastian Guerrero, along with assistant coaches Buck Carraway and Trey Lloyd, is working with the girls to secure what could be the biggest win in a decade—and they’re not alone in their ambitions. The 12U Girls Softball team, the Groesbeck Stone Legends, is also in the hunt for a state title, competing in a tournament in Clifton during the same week. They are led by Head Coach Jerod Stone and Assistant Coach Greg Truett. Meanwhile, from July 11–13, the high school–eligible team will compete for a state title in Corsicana. That squad is led by Head Coach Jason Pringle, with assistance from Sebastian Guerrero and Buck Carraway. Amid this exciting summer of championship dreams, Assistant Coach Buck Carraway also expressed enthusiasm about the broader future of Groesbeck softball. In addition to the new athletic director hired in January, the district recently announced a new head coach for the high school team: Kiley Persons, a Teague High School graduate who played collegiate softball at Howard Payne University while earning both her bachelor’s and master’s degrees. Joining her is new assistant coach Leigh Waller, returning to the Goat family after two years at Mart Elementary. Waller also played college softball at Sam Houston State University. “Many people are working together to put Groesbeck on the softball map,” said Carraway. “I may be biased, but I think each of these teams has a real chance to win their tournaments.”
